example_input: Summarize the changes in this repo
note: Trace reconstructed from the pinned source (no live run). All module links pin the v0.63.0 SHA.

steps.narrative: The Ink TUI captures 'Summarize the changes in this repo'; submitQuery calls GeminiClient.sendMessageStream. BeforeAgent hooks fire once per prompt_id (dedup-guarded via hookStateMap) — a hook can stop the turn, block it, or inject <hook_context> into the request. The client is a thin orchestrator: it does not decide the model, the tools, or the policy — it sequences the specialists that do.
steps.representation:
user text
  -> submitQuery(request, prompt_id)
  -> sendMessageStream(request, signal, prompt_id)
  -> fireBeforeAgentEvent(prompt_id)  # once per prompt, dedup-guarded
  -> hook decisions: continue / stop / inject context
steps.title: Input

steps.narrative: processTurn increments the session turn counter (bails with MaxSessionTurns if the session cap is exceeded), renders history through the context manager (or the legacy compression path if over threshold), and computes boundedTurns = min(turns, MAX_TURNS) with MAX_TURNS = 100. Budgets are enforced before the model is ever consulted — the turn either has budget or it does not.
steps.representation:
processTurn(request, signal, prompt_id, turns)
  -> sessionTurnCount++  # MaxSessionTurns bail
  -> contextManager.renderHistory()  # or legacy compress
  -> boundedTurns = min(turns, 100)  # MAX_TURNS
  -> turn budget remaining: boundedTurns - 1
steps.title: Turn budget

steps.narrative: loopDetector.turnStarted() checks for repeated prompt patterns before the model is called. A detected loop aborts with LoopDetected — the harness refuses to spend another model call on a turn it has already seen. This is the cheap guard; the expensive guard (the next-speaker LLM check) comes after the turn.
steps.representation:
loopDetector.turnStarted()
  -> pattern match over recent prompts
  -> LoopDetected  # abort before any model call
  -> otherwise: proceed to routing
steps.title: Loop guard

steps.narrative: The composite strategy chain routes the model for THIS turn: Fallback → Override → ApprovalMode → Classifiers → Default, first decision wins. The decision (model, source strategy, latency, reasoning) is telemetry-logged as a ModelRoutingEvent, so routing is auditable after the fact. Unless a sequence model is sticky from a previous turn, every turn re-routes — the model answering turn N+1 can differ from turn N by design. setTools(modelToUse) then refreshes model-dependent tool declarations.
steps.representation:
router.route(routingContext)
  -> FallbackStrategy | OverrideStrategy
  -> ApprovalModeStrategy | ClassifierStrategy
  -> DefaultStrategy  # first decision wins
  -> ModelRoutingEvent {model, strategy, reasoning}
  -> setTools(modelToUse)  # refresh declarations
steps.title: Route the model

steps.narrative: Turn.run streams one model call and yields typed events: Thought, Content, ToolCallRequest (one per function call), Citation, Finished. BeforeModel hooks fire during request preparation and can rewrite the model, config, or contents; AfterModel hooks see each streamed chunk and can replace it. The model emits text plus a run_shell_command call (git log --oneline -10). Function-call IDs are synthesized as name__rawCallId when the API does not supply one.
steps.representation:
turn.run(modelToUse)
  -> fireBeforeModelEvent  # hooks may rewrite request
  -> GeminiChat.sendMessageStream -> Gemini API
  -> fireAfterModelEvent  # per chunk; hooks may replace
  -> yield ToolCallRequest {run_shell_command}
  -> call id: run_shell_command__<rawId>
steps.title: Model call

steps.narrative: The CLI collects ToolCallRequest events and useToolScheduler.scheduleToolCalls hands them to the core scheduler. Each call enters the lifecycle at Validating and moves through Scheduled to executing and then a terminal state. The scheduler is the hub: it sequences BeforeTool hooks, policy checks, taint escalation, and confirmation before anything executes.
steps.representation:
scheduleToolCalls([run_shell_command])
  -> CoreToolScheduler._processQueue()
  -> state: Validating -> Scheduled -> executing
  -> terminal: success | error | cancelled
steps.title: Schedule

steps.narrative: _processToolCall runs the gauntlet: BeforeTool hook first (can rewrite args, flagged inputModifiedByHook, or force ask), then PolicyEngine.check (TOML tiers, first match wins — run_shell_command matches the write policy's ask_user rule), then taint-risk escalation (git commands outside the workspace force ASK_USER), then resolveConfirmation publishes TOOL_CONFIRMATION_REQUEST on the message bus with a correlation ID. The bus re-runs the policy engine, then emits to the TUI dialog. The user picks proceed_once; a proceed_always choice would publish UPDATE_POLICY, persisting an autosaved TOML rule.
steps.representation:
_processToolCall
  -> BeforeTool hook  # may rewrite args
  -> checkPolicy -> ASK_USER  # write.toml rule
  -> taint escalation  # git outside workspace?
  -> TOOL_CONFIRMATION_REQUEST {correlationId}
  -> TUI dialog -> outcome: proceed_once
  -> (proceed_always -> UPDATE_POLICY -> TOML)
steps.title: Approval

steps.narrative: The tool executes; output is truncated if over threshold and converted to functionResponse parts. handleCompletedTools calls submitQuery(responses, {isContinuation: true}), re-entering sendMessageStream with boundedTurns - 1. The model summarizes the git log. When a turn ends with no tool calls, the next-speaker LLM check decides whether the model continues ('Please continue.') or the turn ends — the loop's expensive guard, complementing the cheap loop detector from step 3.
steps.representation:
tool.execute() -> output
  -> truncate if over threshold
  -> functionResponse parts
  -> submitQuery(responses, isContinuation:true)
  -> sendMessageStream (boundedTurns - 1)
  -> ... model summarizes ...
  -> checkNextSpeaker: done | 'Please continue.'
steps.title: Execute and continue
